title: Worked Example: A Classical First Movement
welcome_lead: Bar by bar through a Mozart sonata exposition.
final_note: Analysis trains the ear by way of the eye.

walkthroughs.body_html: For a typical Classical first movement: 1st subject (bars 1-20), transition (21-40), 2nd subject (41-60), closing/codetta (61-80). Numbers vary; principle is constant.
The Classical sentence (Schoenberg/Caplin) is 2+2+4: a 2-bar idea, its repeat, then 4 bars of continuation/cadence. Mozart and Haydn use it constantly.
Strong answers cite bar numbers, identify key, name cadence type at each section boundary, and discuss orchestration changes that mark form. Quote precisely.
